newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kobe, Mobil say developing new process for plastic.
newsitem.headline: Kobe, Mobil say developing new process for plastic.

text.p: Kobe Steel Ltd and Mobil Corp said on Wednesday that they are jointly developing a process that could lower the cost of producing 2,6 dimethyl-naphtalene, an intermediate product of polyethylene-naphthalate (PEN), a type of plastic.
Kobe Steel and Mobil are discussing the future development, including commercialisation, of the process, the companies said in a joint statement.

PEN made from 2,6 DMN is drawing increasing attention as a potential replacement for polyethylene terephthalate (PET), which is used to make various products, including fibres, beverage containers, videotapes, photographic film and plastic wrap, they said. PEN is stronger and more heat-resistant than PET, they said.
There are already several ways of making intermediate products for PEN but they are all costly, they said.
